title: More isn't more (Avot 2:7)
hook: more flesh, more worms; more possessions, more worry; more Torah, more life

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hillel spoke to a skull on the water and warned about the circle of revenge. Your line was harm comes back.

The shoes, the gadget, the bigger apartment: the thing someone really wanted, finally bought. For a few days, it was wonderful. Then, quietly, it came with things. A password to remember. A warranty to register. A thing to insure, to clean, to worry about scratching. A rented storage unit is a monument to this feeling. Hillel noticed it too, and turned it into a saying with a beat. It sounds almost like a chant.
screen: `THE THING YOU REALLY WANTED.` → `IT CAME WITH THINGS.` → `A SAYING LIKE A CHANT.`

segments.voice: Here's how his list begins. More flesh, more worms. More possessions, more worry. It's blunt. A body fattened on luxury ends in the same grave as everyone else's, and the more you own, the more you have to guard. In Hebrew it has a beat: marbeh nekhasim, marbeh de'agah. The list goes on through the households of his ancient world, with a few lines about servants and wives that read uncomfortably today, and are honestly part of the text. Then the list turns. More Torah, more life. More sitting in study, more wisdom. More counsel, more understanding. More tzedakah, giving to those in need, more peace. Hillel isn't against more. Some kinds of more shrink you, and some kinds grow you. Possessions pile up and need guarding. Wisdom, understanding and generosity pile up and set you free. And the surprise: giving looks like it should leave a person with less. Hillel says it leaves you with more peace. Then one more line: a person who has gained a good name has gained it for himself, but a person who has gained words of Torah has gained life in the world to come. A good name is precious, he seems to say, but it stays here. What you learn and give goes further. More isn't more. The question is always: more of what?
screen: `MORE FLESH, MORE WORMS.` · `MORE THINGS, MORE WORRY.` · `THE LIST TURNS: MORE TORAH, MORE LIFE.` · `MORE GIVING, MORE PEACE.` · then, large: `MORE ISN'T MORE.`

segments.voice: Picture walking slowly through your home, a closet, a drawer, a shelf, and find one thing you keep but don't need that someone else could use: a coat, a book, a pan. Notice the small tug of wanting to keep it. Then picture it in someone else's hands, being useful, and see if the tug loosens.
Marbeh de'agah. More possessions, more worry: the beat of Hillel's list, before it turns to more learning, more life, and more giving, more peace.
Your line: more giving, more peace. The whole list runs on one word, marbeh. Day two hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: Giving tzedakah, charity understood as justice, is a central Jewish practice, and some households keep a tzedakah box and drop coins in before Shabbat.

notes: Avot is paraphrased (outline follows Taylor 1897). Numbering: 2:7 common, 2:8 in some editions.
The script names but does not recite the lines about wives, maidservants and manservants; a Keeper may prefer a different handling.
'Every storage unit in America' is a light image, not a statistic.
